question: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, ascetic Hindu monk and social reformer of 16th century, was from which of the following States?
solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chaitanya Mahaprabhu** was born on **18 February 1486** in Nabadwip, West Bengal, which is currently in India.
 
• He is considered an **incarnation of Lord Krishna** by his followers and is a revered figure in the Gaudiya Vaishnavism tradition.
 
• Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's teachings emphasize the importance of **devotional worship** (bhakti) of Krishna through the chanting of the Hare Krishna mantra.
 
• He played a significant role in the **Bengal Renaissance** and influenced various social and religious reforms during his time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gaudiya Vaishnavism**: A tradition of Vaishnavism (worship of Vishnu) that was propagated by Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and emphasizes the worship of Krishna.
 
• **Hare Krishna Movement**: Also known as the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON), it was founded in 1966 by A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, drawing inspiration from Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's teachings.
 
• **Bhakti Yoga**: A spiritual practice within Hinduism focusing on loving devotion towards a personal god, popularized by Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.
 
• **Nabadwip**: The birthplace of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, it is a prominent pilgrimage site for his followers and is located in the Nadia district of West Bengal.
 
• **Bengal Renaissance**: A socio-cultural and religious reform movement in the 19th and early 20th centuries in Bengal, influenced by figures like Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, Raja Ram Mohan Roy, and others.
